items.followUp: What is the body section of an HTML document?

rubric.why: Identifies the section and its HTML tags.
rubric.description: States that the head section is the part of an HTML document enclosed by <head> and </head>.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the head section and its tags.

rubric.why: Explains the section’s purpose.
rubric.description: Explains that it contains information about the webpage, such as its title or metadata, which is generally not displayed in the page body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct purpose or example.

modelAnswer: The head section is the part of an HTML document enclosed between the <head> and </head> tags.
It contains information about the webpage, such as its title and metadata, which is generally not displayed in the page body.

rubric.why: Shows that requirements are determined by first understanding the problem.
rubric.description: Understand and clearly define the problem to be solved.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the need to understand or define the problem.

rubric.why: Identifies the information supplied to the solution.
rubric.description: Determine the required input data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying inputs.

rubric.why: Identifies what the solution must produce.
rubric.description: Determine the expected output or result.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying outputs.

rubric.why: Identifies what must happen to transform the inputs into the required outputs.
rubric.description: Determine the processing steps, calculations, conditions, and relevant constraints.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the processing or other relevant requirements.

modelAnswer: First, understand and clearly define the problem that the flowchart must solve.
Identify the input data required by the problem.
Identify the expected output or result.
Determine the processing steps, calculations, conditions, and constraints needed to produce the output from the input.

items.followUp: Define the OSI model and explain the function of the data-link layer.

rubric.why: Defines a network model as an organised framework for communication.
rubric.description: Defines a computer network model as a layered framework that describes how devices communicate and how data is transmitted across a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: Gives a correct function of an OSI layer.
rubric.description: The application layer provides network services to applications used by the user.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct explanation of the application layer.

rubric.why: Gives a correct function of an OSI layer.
rubric.description: The transport layer manages end-to-end delivery of data, including dividing it into segments and supporting reliable delivery.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct explanation of the transport layer.

rubric.why: Gives a correct function of an OSI layer.
rubric.description: The network layer selects routes and forwards packets toward their destination, using logical addressing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct explanation of the network layer.

modelAnswer: A computer network model is a layered framework that explains how devices communicate and how data is transmitted over a network.
The application layer provides network services to applications used by the user.
The transport layer manages end-to-end delivery of data and may divide it into segments for transmission.
The network layer selects routes and forwards packets toward their destination using logical addresses.

items.followUp: What is phishing? Explain how it can be used to commit cybercrime.

rubric.why: Defines cybercrime as unlawful activity involving computers or networks.
rubric.description: Cybercrime is an illegal activity carried out using a computer, digital device, or network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: Identifies and explains a common type of cybercrime.
rubric.description: Hacking means gaining unauthorised access to a computer or network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one type with a correct explanation.

rubric.why: Identifies another type and its purpose.
rubric.description: Phishing uses deceptive messages or websites to steal personal information; identity theft involves misusing someone’s personal details.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct type with an explanation.

rubric.why: Identifies a further type of cybercrime and explains it.
rubric.description: Gives another valid type, such as cyberstalking, malware attacks, software piracy, online fraud, or cyberbullying, with a suitable explanation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one further valid type with an explanation.

modelAnswer: Cybercrime is an illegal activity carried out using a computer, digital device, or network.
Hacking is gaining unauthorised access to a computer or network.
Phishing uses deceptive messages or websites to obtain a person’s private information.
Other types include identity theft, cyberstalking, malware attacks, online fraud, software piracy, and cyberbullying.

items.followUp: Explain the top-down and bottom-up approaches to planning a solution.

rubric.why: Names a valid solution-planning strategy.
rubric.description: Identifies the top-down strategy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming top-down.

rubric.why: Names a second valid solution-planning strategy.
rubric.description: Identifies the bottom-up strategy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming bottom-up.

modelAnswer: Top-down strategy: divide a large problem into smaller, manageable sub-problems and solve them step by step.
Bottom-up strategy: develop and combine small components to build the complete solution.

items.followUp: State two ways a flowchart can help when checking an algorithm.

rubric.why: Recognises that a flowchart presents solution steps visually.
rubric.description: A flowchart gives a visual or graphical representation of the steps in a solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing its visual representation of steps.

rubric.why: States a practical benefit in problem solving.
rubric.description: It helps users understand or communicate the logic and can help find errors in the solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid benefit.

modelAnswer: A flowchart shows the steps of a solution visually, making the problem-solving logic easier to understand.
It helps communicate the solution and can make errors or missing steps easier to find.

items.followUp: What three things should be identified when analysing a problem?

rubric.why: Describes problem analysis as careful study of the problem.
rubric.description: Problem analysis is the careful study and understanding of a problem before designing its solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the study or understanding of the problem.

rubric.why: Shows the purpose of analysis: identifying what is needed to solve the problem.
rubric.description: It identifies the required inputs, processing, and outputs or other requirements of the problem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying these requirements.

modelAnswer: Problem analysis is the careful study and understanding of a problem before designing its solution.
It identifies the problem’s required inputs, processing, and expected outputs.

items.followUp: What is meant by space complexity of an algorithm?

rubric.why: Identifies time as one basis for measuring algorithm efficiency.
rubric.description: Time complexity is based on the time or number of operations an algorithm needs as the input size changes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying execution time or operations as a metric.

rubric.why: Identifies memory use as the other basis for measuring algorithm efficiency.
rubric.description: Space complexity is based on the memory or storage an algorithm needs as the input size changes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying memory or storage use as a metric.

modelAnswer: Time complexity measures the time or number of operations an algorithm needs as the input size changes.
Space complexity measures the memory or storage an algorithm needs as the input size changes.
